narrative.summary: Germany implemented the EU AI Act through the KI-MIG, in force since 29 July 2026, which makes the Federal Network Agency the default market surveillance authority, single point of contact and host of the national AI sandbox, with BaFin supervising AI in financial services and Länder authorities covering Länder bodies and media. Federal policy rests on the 2018 AI strategy and its 2020 update, the 2023 AI Action Plan, the 2025 Hightech Agenda with a 2026 AI roadmap, the 2026 National Data Centre Strategy and 2025 guidelines for AI use in the federal administration, with ministries adding their own AI documents (Interior, Foreign Office, Labour, Defence, Health and a federal–Länder justice AI strategy). Other federal law touching AI includes the Federal Data Protection Act's scoring and automated-decision rules (reformed with effect from November 2026), the health data law allowing AI training on research data, and automated and autonomous driving rules. Regulators are prolific: the Data Protection Conference and the Federal Data Protection Commissioner issue AI guidance, BaFin sets expectations for algorithms and AI risks in finance, the BSI publishes extensive AI security criteria and guidance, and the Federal Network Agency has issued AI literacy guidance. Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, North Rhine-Westphalia and Berlin have police laws expressly regulating automated or AI data analysis, Berlin's e-government act requires notification of new AI systems, and Hesse has AI strategies for the economy and its administration.

narrative.review_notes: A deep review completed on 11 October 2026 searched, in German and English, federal laws and ordinances, the federal government and ministries, federal regulators, national standards and the Länder of Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Berlin and Hesse; EU and Council of Europe instruments, including the AI Act, are listed in the regional pages, and bills are listed as pending rather than as documents. Some official websites, including the economy ministry, the justice ministry and the medicines regulator's search, were unavailable and national standards were checked only from their catalogue entries; pending are the deepfake offence (§ 201b of the Criminal Code) and the government's draft law on digital violence, the federal police data-analysis bill, the AI sandbox ordinance under the KI-MIG, Hesse's police data-analysis provision and unpublished internal AI rules of federal ministries.

instruments.current_status: In use across the federal administration. The government publication portal lists the brochure (article no. BMI25020) with 'Stand: 27. The federal government's answer of 30 July 2026 (Bundestag printed paper 21/7443) confirms the guidelines remain the general framework, supplemented by ministry- and agency-specific rules.
instruments.summary: Cross-government guidelines setting general guard-rails for AI use in the federal administration: five value-based guiding principles (opportunity-oriented and responsible use, human-centred use, trustworthy AI systems, supporting staff and building skills, sustainable joint deployment) and 14 'Leitsätze': five for users (responsible use, minimising data disclosure, careful data input, checking AI output, transparent use) and nine for authorities, such as clear decisions on use, defining purpose and scope, choosing suitable systems, skills offers, transparency about AI use and data-protection-compliant deployment. An annex gives practical guidance on large language models, including prompting and hallucination risks. They follow the EU AI Act definition and risk-based approach and favour open models to preserve digital sovereignty.

instruments.official_title: Gesetz zur Marktüberwachung und Innovationsförderung von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI-Marktüberwachungs-und-Innovationsförderungs-Gesetz – KI-MIG)
instruments.english_title: Act on Market Surveillance and Innovation Promotion for Artificial Intelligence (AI Market Surveillance and Innovation Promotion Act – KI-MIG)
instruments.issuing_authority: Bundestag (government bill of the Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation)
instruments.publisher_name: Federal Ministry of Justice and Consumer Protection
instruments.current_status: In force since 29 July 2026. Enacted as Article 1 of the 'Gesetz zur Durchführung der Verordnung über künstliche Intelligenz' of 22 July 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 223, issued 28 July 2026; Article 5: in force the day after promulgation). Procedure: BMDS draft sent to Länder and associations on 12 September 2025; cabinet decision 11 February 2026; government bill BT-Drs. 21/4594 (9 March 2026); Bundesrat opinion of 27 March 2026 (BT-Drs. 21/5143); first reading 20 March 2026, hearing 23 March 2026; Bundestag adopted it with amendments on 11 June 2026 (committee report BT-Drs. 21/6407); Bundesrat (1067th session, 10 July 2026, BR-Drs. 375/26) did not call the mediation committee. The BMDS procedure page cites 'BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 233'; the Federal Law Gazette itself gives Nr. 223. No implementing ordinance under § 13(4) (AI regulatory sandboxes) was found as of October 2026.
instruments.summary: Germany's national implementing law for the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It makes the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) the default market surveillance authority, single point of contact and central complaints office, gives BaFin market surveillance of AI used in regulated financial activities, keeps existing product-sector authorities for Annex I products, leaves Länder public bodies and media to Länder authorities, and creates an independent AI Market Surveillance Chamber within BNetzA for high-risk AI in law enforcement, migration/border control, justice and democracy, plus a Coordination and Competence Centre with a federal–Länder AI committee. It also obliges BNetzA to run at least one AI regulatory sandbox and provide innovation support, sets approval (deemed after 30 days) for real-world testing of high-risk AI, fines of up to EUR 50,000 for certain deployer and fundamental-rights-impact-assessment breaches (no fines on public bodies), a non-public register for critical-infrastructure high-risk systems and evaluations after 18 months and three years; the enacting act also adds AI Act breaches to the Whistleblower Protection Act and amends SGB I and the FinDAG.

instruments.summary: Germany's first national AI strategy ('AI made in Germany'), drawn up after a nationwide online consultation, with 12 fields of action covering research, innovation clusters, transfer to SMEs, start-ups, labour market and skills, AI for sovereign tasks in public administration, data availability, the regulatory framework, standards, national and international networking and societal dialogue. It set the goals of making Germany and Europe a leading AI location, ensuring responsible and public-good-oriented AI development and use, and embedding AI ethically, legally and culturally in society, with an announced federal budget of around EUR 3 billion to 2025.

instruments.publisher_name: State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information Baden-Württemberg
instruments.current_status: Updated version 2.0 of 17 October 2024, revised after feedback from practitioners; it is the current version on the LfDI website as of October 2026.
instruments.summary: The LfDI BW discussion paper asks when and how personal data may be processed for training and applying AI. It distinguishes the processing phases from collecting training data to using AI outputs, allocates controller, joint-controller and processor responsibility, and examines each GDPR legal basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, public task, legitimate interests) plus specific national bases for public and non-public bodies, including Baden-Württemberg Land law for the public sector.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land DPA's main AI guidance on legal bases for processing personal data in AI training and use.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11. Status note: Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): PDF cover: 'Version 2.0 vom 17.10.2024'.

instruments.official_title: Gesetz zur Einführung einer automatisierten Datenanalyse und zur Änderung weiterer polizeirechtlicher Vorschriften vom 18. November 2025
instruments.english_title: Act introducing automated data analysis and amending further police-law provisions of 18 November 2025
instruments.issuing_authority: Landtag von Baden-Württemberg; Landesregierung Baden-Württemberg (GBl. 2025 Nr. 117)
instruments.current_status: Passed by the Landtag on 12 November 2025, signed 18 November 2025, promulgated in GBl. 2025 Nr. 117 of 2 December 2025; in force on the day after promulgation (3 December 2025). Later amendments to the Police Act (2026) not checked.
instruments.summary: The Act inserts § 47a into the Baden-Württemberg Police Act, allowing the police to merge, link, match, prepare, evaluate and assess personal data from police filing systems on an analysis platform (automated data analysis) to avert specified dangers and prevent serious offences, subject to an access-rights concept, data categorisation that excludes uninvolved persons' case data, a leadership order and prior consultation of the LfDI. It also inserts § 57a permitting police to further process existing personal data to develop, train, test, validate and monitor information-technology products. The text does not use the term artificial intelligence.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land police law authorising automated data analysis platforms and the use of police data to train and test IT products.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11

instruments.official_title: Achtes Gesetz zur Änderung des Polizeigesetzes des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen vom 2. Dezember 2025
instruments.english_title: Eighth Act amending the Police Act of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia of 2 December 2025
instruments.issuing_authority: Landtag Nordrhein-Westfalen; Landesregierung Nordrhein-Westfalen (GV. NRW. 2025 S. 1132)
instruments.current_status: Signed 2 December 2025, promulgated in GV. NRW. 2025 Nr. 48 of 12 December 2025 (p. 1132); in force on the day after promulgation (13 December 2025). The consolidated PolG NRW of 13.12.2025 on recht.nrw.de includes the new provisions.
instruments.summary: The Act amends § 23 of the NRW Police Act so that, beyond automated merging of lawfully stored data, the police may run data analyses that establish relationships between persons, groups, institutions, objects and things and statistically evaluate stored data, for specified purposes and only case-related by qualified, authorised staff under an authorisation concept. Where self-operating or self-learning systems are used, it must be ensured that discriminatory algorithms are neither used nor developed and, as far as technically possible, that the procedure is traceable; automated individual decisions under § 46 of the NRW Data Protection Act are excluded.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land police law expressly regulating automated and self-learning data analysis systems.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11

instruments.official_title: Gesetz zur Änderung des E-Government-Gesetzes Berlin, des Rechnungshofgesetzes und des Berliner Datenschutzgesetzes vom 23. Februar 2026
instruments.english_title: Act amending the Berlin E-Government Act, the Court of Audit Act and the Berlin Data Protection Act of 23 February 2026
instruments.issuing_authority: Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin (GVBl. 2026 Nr. 7, S. 78)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated in GVBl. Nr. 7 of 6 March 2026; in force on the day after promulgation (7 March 2026). Senate Chancellery circular Nr. 1/2026 of 12 May 2026 informs the administration of its entry into force and of the plan to use the federal MaKI platform as the transparency register for notified AI systems.
instruments.summary: The Act inserts § 16a 'Einsatz von KI-Systemen' into the Berlin E-Government Act: introducing an AI system must be notified to the ICT steering unit (except where security authorities' confidentiality interests prevent it), and authorities may process personal data, including special-category data, in AI systems where they are otherwise authorised to process it, the input is necessary, the data do not alter the AI model and risk-mitigating measures ensure data minimisation, confidentiality, transparency and related principles. Users must be informed before deployment; a new § 13a of the Court of Audit Act extends the rules to the Rechnungshof.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land law creating a dedicated legal basis and notification duty for AI systems in the public administration.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11

instruments.official_title: Gesetz zur Reform des Berliner Polizei- und Ordnungsrechts und zur Änderung des Gesetzes zu Artikel 29 der Verfassung von Berlin vom 11. Dezember 2025
instruments.english_title: Act reforming Berlin police and public-order law and amending the Act on Article 29 of the Constitution of Berlin of 11 December 2025
instruments.issuing_authority: Abgeordnetenhaus von Berlin (GVBl. 2025 Nr. 36, S. 590)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated in GVBl. Nr. 36 of 23 December 2025; in force on the day after promulgation (24 December 2025), except Article 2 (1 January 2031). A challenge before the Berlin Constitutional Court was reported in the press (not verified on an official source).
instruments.summary: The reform rewrites the Berlin Security and Public Order Act (ASOG). New § 42d allows police and fire services to further process stored personal data to train and test AI systems serving their tasks, requiring that discriminatory algorithms are neither developed nor used, priority for anonymised or pseudonymised data, deletion deadlines and safeguards against re-identification. New § 47a authorises an automated application for analysing existing data, expressly permitting self-learning systems only under stricter conditions (e.g. terrorist or serious offences) and on order of the head of the State Criminal Police Office, with selected trained staff, a role and rights concept and logging.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land police law expressly regulating AI training with police data and self-learning analysis systems.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11

instruments.official_title: KI-Strategie für die Hessische Landesverwaltung
instruments.english_title: AI Strategy for the Hessian State Administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Hessisches Ministerium für Digitalisierung und Innovation
instruments.current_status: Published as the first edition, dated August 2026 ('Stand: August 2026'); a first AI action plan for 2026 is announced to be published alongside and updated continuously. An evaluation is planned for 2028.
instruments.summary: The strategy sets the vision that by 2030 the Hessian Land administration should be a pioneer in safe and responsible AI use, with guiding principles including human responsibility for administrative action, data protection, information security, non-discrimination and digital sovereignty. It defines three fields of action — AI competence (needs-based staff training), AI tools (a sovereign, interoperable product portfolio on the Land multi-cloud platform) and AI governance (use of existing committee structures, a quality-assurance system, continuous monitoring and the common model rule on generative AI) — to be operationalised in a rolling AI action plan.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Land AI strategy for the public administration of Hesse.

instruments.official_title: Regelung zum Umgang mit im Internet verfügbaren Systemen der generativen Künstlichen Intelligenz im Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt
instruments.english_title: Rule on the use of internet-available generative AI systems at the Darmstadt Regional Council
instruments.issuing_authority: Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt
instruments.current_status: Internal rule dated 8 October 2025 addressed to all staff of the Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt; a first evaluation is foreseen six months after announcement.
instruments.summary: Binding internal rule for staff of the Darmstadt Regional Council (a Hessian Land authority) and its contractors on using internet-available generative AI systems: official decisions remain with humans, outputs must be checked for accuracy and discrimination, and users remain responsible. Use is allowed in principle via a positive list of vetted tools, tools on a negative list are prohibited, new tools need prior information-security and data-protection review, and entering personal data, trade secrets and other protected information is restricted; it references the AI Act's Art. 4 literacy and Art. 5 prohibitions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Authority-level binding staff rule on generative AI in a Hessian Land authority.
instruments.evidence_reference: deu-deep-review-D4-2026-10-11

organizations.name: Federal Government
organizations.ai_governance_role: Federal Government of Germany (Bundesregierung); adopts cross-government strategies by cabinet decision (AI strategy 2018 and its 2020 update, Hightech Agenda Deutschland 2025, Modernisation Agenda 2025, National Data Centre Strategy 2026).

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
organizations.ai_governance_role: Federal research ministry (BMFTR; until May 2025 the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, BMBF). Co-lead of the 2018 AI strategy, author of the 2023 AI Action Plan, lead ministry for the Hightech Agenda Deutschland and its AI technology roadmap.

organizations.name: Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation
organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for the national implementation of the EU AI Act (KI-MIG draft, consultation and government bill); responsible under § 6(5) KI-MIG for the reporting obligation under Article 70(6) AI Act and empowered by § 13(4) KI-MIG to regulate AI regulatory sandboxes by ordinance.

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of the Interior
organizations.ai_governance_role: Federal interior ministry (BMI). Issued, with the Federal Government Commissioner for Information Technology, the 2025 Guidelines for the Use of AI in the Federal Administration and the 2024 AI mission statement for its portfolio; published the Data Ethics Commission report (2019).

organizations.name: Federal Foreign Office
organizations.ai_governance_role: Foreign ministry (Auswärtiges Amt). Issued the AI Charter for the Federal Foreign Office (2024).

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Labour and social affairs ministry (BMAS); co-lead of the 2018 AI strategy; its Digital Labour Society think tank (Denkfabrik) coordinated the self-binding AI guidelines for the labour and social administration (2022).

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of Defence
organizations.ai_governance_role: Defence ministry (BMVg). Issued the AI concept K-9000/102 for its portfolio (2026); the Army Concepts and Capabilities Development Centre published an AI position paper (2019).

organizations.name: Federal Ministry of Health
organizations.ai_governance_role: Health ministry (BMG). Issues the digitalisation strategy for health and care, updated in 2026 with an AI focus.

organizations.name: Data Ethics Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Expert commission set up by the Federal Government on 18 July 2018 to develop ethical standards and recommendations on data and algorithmic systems; delivered its report on 23 October 2019 (concluded).

organizations.name: E-Justice Council
organizations.ai_governance_role: E-Justice-Rat: body of the heads of the federal and Länder justice administrations that coordinates IT and digitalisation in the justice system; adopted the joint AI strategy for the justice system (2025).

organizations.name: Data Protection Conference
organizations.ai_governance_role: Conference of the independent federal and Länder data protection supervisory authorities (DSK). Adopts resolutions (Entschließungen), decisions and guidance (Orientierungshilfen) on AI and data protection, including the 2019 Hambach Declaration, the May 2024 guidance on AI and data protection, the June 2025 guidance on technical and organisational measures for AI systems and the October 2025 guidance on RAG systems.

organizations.name: Federal Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information
organizations.ai_governance_role: Federal data protection supervisory authority for federal public bodies and telecoms/postal services. Issues AI guidance for federal authorities (2025 handout on AI in authorities, 2024 handout for security authorities), ran public consultations on AI in law enforcement (2021) and on personal data in AI models (2025), and takes part in the trilateral AI regulatory sandbox pilot with the Federal Network Agency and Hesse.

organizations.name: Federal Financial Supervisory Authority
organizations.ai_governance_role: AI Act market surveillance authority under § 2(3) KI-MIG for AI systems directly connected to regulated financial activities of the institutions and insurers it supervises; sets its own cybersecurity testing requirements for high-risk AI in consultation with BNetzA (§ 10(2) KI-MIG).

organizations.name: Federal Office for Information Security
organizations.ai_governance_role: Under §§ 3(2) and 10(4) KI-MIG acts, until the Cyber Resilience Act market surveillance authority is designated, as notifying authority for Annex III No. 1 (biometric) high-risk AI systems and as cooperation partner on AI cybersecurity requirements.

organizations.name: Federal Network Agency
organizations.ai_governance_role: Default AI Act market surveillance authority under § 2(1) KI-MIG and single point of contact (§ 6), central complaints office (§ 8), host of the Coordination and Competence Centre for the AI Act (§ 5), the independent AI Market Surveillance Chamber for law-enforcement, migration/border, justice and democracy high-risk systems (§§ 2(5), 4), the national AI regulatory sandbox (§ 13), the non-public register of Annex III No. 2 high-risk systems (§ 20) and innovation support including the AI Service Desk (§ 12).

organizations.name: German Institute for Standardization
organizations.ai_governance_role: National standards body (DIN e. V.); adopts European and international AI standards as DIN EN / DIN ISO standards through committee NA 043-01-42 (Artificial Intelligence).

organizations.name: Bundestag
organizations.ai_governance_role: Federal parliament (Deutscher Bundestag). Enacts federal laws with AI provisions, including the KI-MIG (adopted 11 June 2026), the BDSG and its 2026 scoring reform, the GDNG and the automated/autonomous driving amendments to the Road Traffic Act; receives the annual activity report of the BNetzA AI Market Surveillance Chamber and the government's KI-MIG evaluation reports.

organizations.name: Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport
organizations.ai_governance_role: Issued the 2022 Autonomous Vehicles Approval and Operation Ordinance (AFGBV) under § 1j StVG; its transport portfolio is now held by the Federal Ministry of Transport.

organizations.name: Free State of Bavaria
organizations.ai_governance_role: Bavarian State Government and ministries; the State Ministry of Finance and Home Affairs (digital administration) issues the staff AI guide; the Landtag enacts Land law such as the Police Tasks Act.

organizations.name: Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision
organizations.ai_governance_role: Data protection supervisory authority for the private sector in Bavaria (BayLDA); publishes an AI checklist with GDPR test criteria.

organizations.name: Bavarian State Commissioner for Data Protection
organizations.ai_governance_role: Data protection supervisory authority for Bavarian public bodies (BayLfD); publishes guidance on data protection in AI projects of the Bavarian administration.

organizations.name: State of Baden-Württemberg
organizations.ai_governance_role: Land government of Baden-Württemberg (Landesregierung, Ministry of the Interior, Digitalisation and Local Government); the Landtag enacts Land law such as the Police Act.

organizations.name: State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information Baden-Württemberg
organizations.ai_governance_role: Data protection supervisory authority of Baden-Württemberg (LfDI BW); publishes the discussion paper on legal bases for processing personal data in AI.

organizations.name: State of North Rhine-Westphalia
organizations.ai_governance_role: Land government of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesregierung; Ministry of the Interior; Ministry for Home Affairs, Local Government, Building and Digitalisation); the Landtag enacts Land law such as the Police Act.
